analytics.disabled_reason: GitHub Pages serves static files. No persistent same-origin runtime, production receipt, approved privacy/retention notice or host-log policy has been verified. The tested client and Python aggregate collector are deployment-ready references, not live analytics.
enable_procedure: Deploy analytics/collector.py behind TLS at the same-origin route /api/analytics/events, with its SQLite volume outside the checkout and access logs disabled or covered by the approved policy.
Verify runtime_selected, endpoint_deployed, privacy_notice_approved, host_logging_reviewed and end_to_end_verified in data/analytics-plan.json. These are evidence gates, not defaults to bypass.

Enable both data/config.json analytics.enabled and data/analytics-plan.json collection.enabled in one reviewed change. Use the same-origin /api/analytics/events endpoint. Rebuild: privacy wording changes from the same switch.
Run the browser/HTTP contract tests, then confirm an authorized production diagnostic reaches the aggregate store. Keep diagnostics separate from campaign data. Never simulate clicks to Amazon.
Import EV-05 only from an authorized first-party aggregate report. Missing reported fields remain null; no click-to-order inference is permitted.
never_recorded: cookie or any persistent reader identifier
order value or anything about what the reader bought
analytics.policy_basis: Amazon Program Policies Participation Requirements §3(e) requires accurate privacy/technology disclosure, and §6(s) prohibits artificially generated clicks. Measurement only observes reader activations; it neither visits Amazon automatically nor changes any destination.
analytics.event_definitions: data/analytics-plan.json is canonical; data/measurement.json must match exactly. Four browser triggers plus one operator-only authorized aggregate import.
